definitions.gloss: charm against evil; talisman; protective ward; amulet
definitions.explanation: An object, symbol, or practice believed to protect against evil spirits, bad luck, or misfortune. Encompasses physical objects like talismans and decorations, as well as customs and rituals performed for protection.

examples.japanese: {玄関|げんかん}に{魔除|まよ}けを{飾|かざ}った。
examples.english: I placed a protective charm at the entrance.

examples.japanese: この{石|いし}は{魔除|まよ}けの{効果|こうか}があると{言|い}われている。
examples.english: This stone is said to have protective powers against evil.

examples.japanese: {節分|せつぶん}に{柊|ひいらぎ}と{鰯|いわし}の{頭|あたま}を{飾|かざ}るのは、{古|ふる}くからの{魔除|まよ}けの{風習|ふうしゅう}だ。
examples.english: Decorating with holly and sardine heads at Setsubun is an ancient custom for warding off evil.

notes:
Composed of {魔|ま} (demon, evil spirit) + {除|よ}け (warding off, protection). The suffix 〜{除|よ}け is productive and appears in other protective compounds.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {魔除|まよ}けの{効果|こうか}: evil-warding effect
- {魔除|まよ}けのお{守|まも}り: protective amulet
- {魔除|まよ}けの{風習|ふうしゅう}: evil-warding custom
- {魔除|まよ}けを{飾|かざ}る: to display a protective charm

RELATED WORDS WITH 〜{除|よ}け:
- {虫除|むしよ}け: insect repellent
- {日除|ひよ}け: sunshade, parasol
- {雨除|あまよ}け: rain shelter

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, common {魔除|まよ}け items include {鬼瓦|おにがわら} (demon-faced roof tiles), {注連縄|しめなわ} (sacred Shinto ropes), and {鏡|かがみ} (mirrors). {獅子舞|ししまい} (lion dances) performed at festivals also serve as {魔除|まよ}け.
